newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CanWest to sell part of Ten to TNQ - paper.
newsitem.headline: CanWest to sell part of Ten to TNQ - paper.

text.p: Canadian media group CanWest Global Communications Corp is set to sell an 18.5 percent stake in Australia's Ten television network to Telecasters North Queensland (TNQ) Ltd, The Sydney Morning Herald newspaper reported on Thursday.
The government has ruled CanWest must cut its 76 percent stake in Ten down to a previously sanctioned level of 57.5 percent.
TNQ, which already has a 20 percent economic interest and a 40 percent voting interest in Ten, would then become the vehicle for a public float of Ten, the newspaper said.

"Telecasters North Queensland has become the firm favourite for the float vehicle for Ten Group, with the publicly listed company preparing to sign a memormandum of understanding with Izzy Asper's CanWest," the Herald said.
Asper has been in Australia in the past week, trying to seek a solution to the government demand that CanWest sell its stake to meet foreign ownership regulations.

However, the Australian Broadcasting Authority, the statutory authority administering broadcasting laws and advising the government, also recently said Ten may still be in breach of broadcasting rules even if it reduces its stake to 57.5 percent.
TNQ's shares closed unchanged at A$5.50 on Wednesday.
